g.id: Label criteria out, gaps back [P5, P6]

path.id: Why, how and where context is lost, for the three roles added after the interviews
Backlog priority and the acceptance criteria. [P5, P6]
Criteria are written for the end user, not tied to the codebase architecture, so gaps show up late. [P6]
No specific handoff process. Criteria go out; gaps the engineer finds go back to the PO. [P5]
Decisions made in Slack and in meetings never reach the spec. [P1, P6]
A second look at the code: pull request review, and testing by other developers and the PO. [P6]
They catch what the author and the agent did not. [P6]
Through pull request review and testing, after the code already exists. [P6]
Review depth dropped to skimming as code volume rose. [P2]
Context from other repos and undocumented sources. [P4, P6]
Context across repos cannot fit in one prompt, and the agent cannot see it unless someone attaches it. [P4]
Today the engineer finds the relevant files and attaches them to the chat. [P6]
Undocumented facts (URLs, how auth works) and other repos sit outside the chat. [P4, P6]
